---
title: Bank payouts
description: Add your bank once. The fee for that payout appears before you confirm.
---

You add your bank account once. When you pay out, the fee for that amount appears before you confirm.

## Add the account

Open Pay out. If there is no bank account yet, the screen asks you to add one and opens the bank form. You can also add it from Settings, then Payouts.

Enter the country of the bank, the name on the account, and the account number. A West African account is 24 characters and also needs the bank's SWIFT code. The account should be in the business name. You need a payout PIN first. Adding the account asks for that PIN.

The account is saved turned off. You cannot pay out to it until it is confirmed. A eurozone, UK, or Vietnam account is checked with the bank: a number that does not exist, or a name that is not the business, is refused. West African banks do not publish an account check, so a different name is still saved. The team gets an email to accept or refuse it. A number the bank says does not exist is refused.

A bank in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, or Togo is paid in F CFA. A eurozone bank is paid in euros. A US bank is paid in dollars. You can withdraw XOF, USD, or EUR. If that balance is not the bank's currency, the payout converts at the currency conversion rate in Settings → Fees, typically 1%. You do not convert first as a separate step.

## What you pay

The amount you enter is what leaves that balance. The fee comes out of that amount, and your bank receives the rest in its currency. A balance of 300,000 F CFA can pay out 300,000 F CFA. The fee is shown underneath, and the bank receives 300,000 minus that fee. The payout is not refused because the fee is there.

A bank payout currently charges the **transfer cost** only: the exchange into the bank's currency and the bank network fee. The lomi. share is not added. The fee is calculated when you type the amount, and that exact fee is what you pay.

A local payout to one of those West African banks is in F CFA. The network fee on that local transfer is zero. If you already hold F CFA, there is no exchange on that send. If you withdraw dollars or euros to that bank, the conversion rate above is the fee.

A euro payout to a eurozone bank, or a dollar payout to a US bank, has no exchange and no network fee when you withdraw that same currency, so there is nothing extra to pay. A bank the local networks do not reach is sent by international wire: the transfer cost is the 15 USD wire fee, plus the exchange if the currency changes.

It arrives in 1 to 5 business days. It is not instant.

Each bank payout keeps the transfer cost, the lomi. share (currently 0), and the exchange quote from that send. Those figures are what this page is checked against when the cost changes.

Wave in Côte d'Ivoire is a separate payout, not this bank fee. A saved Wave number is 1%. A number you just added stays on a higher rate for 48 hours, then drops to 1%.

The payout screen shows what you receive, the transfer cost, the lomi. fee, and the total taken from the balance. Confirm only after the fee is on screen. If the fee cannot be calculated, the screen says so and you cannot confirm until it loads.

Through the API, send `currency_code` as `XOF`, `USD`, or `EUR`. If that is not the bank's currency, the payout converts at the currency conversion rate, then pays the bank in its currency. The amount you send is what leaves that balance. The first `POST /payouts` call without `confirmation_token` returns `transfer_amount` (what the bank receives), `transfer_cost_amount`, `lomi_fee_amount`, `fee_amount`, and `total_deduction`. `total_deduction` is that debit. The payout you confirm with the token is priced the same way, at the rate of that moment.
